proofUses.reason: Tonelli and the binomial generating series identify the lazy Green function with twice the ordinary one, transferring the three diagram thresholds without monotone Fourier integrands of mixed sign.

A leave-one-out Jensen argument makes inverse moments nonincreasing in dimension. Pairing opposite walk increments gives the weighted decay; damping is monotone in nonnegative return coefficients at the origin.
Nonnegative inverse coefficients control the first shift. A cosine-sine decomposition and a second nonnegative coefficient sequence control the two shifts; Fatou supplies the critical endpoint.

Fourier positivity and inversion give the diagrams; Cauchy–Schwarz yields the neighbouring triangle. Criticality is reached through nonnegative spatial sums. The infrared bound itself stays a hypothesis.

The one-dimensional Dirichlet kernel gives a quadratic small-frequency bound and a uniform gap outside the small cube. Parseval controls the weighted integral. Subtracting the zero-step and linear terms proves that the full triangle is one plus O(L^(-d)).
The coordinate recurrence counts returns exactly. Symmetry and a Gaussian integral bound give an explicit series tail; leave-one-out Jensen applies to both convex integrands.
Finite rational sums and the proved tail bound certify three pairs of walk norms. The infrared amplitude bounds the sixth connector norm, with all remaining percolation hypotheses retained.

A self-contained dyadic lattice-shell argument: exponential ball-mass growth absorbs fixed logarithmic powers, and the triangle sum partitions by its shortest side. No symmetry or Fourier positivity is used.
Substitution of the Gaussian power alpha=2 gives the distinct bubble and triangle thresholds, including logarithmic and double-logarithmic borderline cases.
A dyadic partition and repeated integration by parts control the local inverse transform; integrable derivatives of the complementary homogeneous symbol justify removing the cutoff off the origin.
Expansion of the exact nearest-neighbour resolvent, the local Fourier remainder bound and Gaussian inverse transforms identify the angular correction with a uniform spatial error.

The generating condition gives the sole quadratic Fourier singularity. A covariance change of variables yields the power coefficient; integrable symbol subtraction and its derivative estimate yield the finite part and marginal remainder.

The nearest-neighbour covariance fixes the logarithmic constants. Differentiation of the bubble resolvent and the triangle finite part give the critical bubble expansion; the mass definition supplies the normalization comparison.

Positive integral identities isolate the frequency difference, covariance rescaling gives an integrable continuum limit, and a parameter integral evaluates its universal profile. The unshifted finite part fixes the additive constant.

A uniformly integrable subtraction at the two distinct singular points transfers the quadratic shifted integral. The parameter integral and marginal radial primitive identify its finite part; KC8U supplies the nearest-neighbour constants.
